title: Con Law II
description: Constitutional Law II: the First Amendment, Chapters 1–6. Covers the Religion Clauses, the speech framework, incitement and national security, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech, including obscenity, child pornography, and indecency.

First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-6_Revised.pd.title: First Amendment Outline
First_Amendment_Outline_Ch1-6_Revised.pd.description: Case-by-case outline of Chapters 1–6, from Barnette and Kennedy v. Bremerton through Counterman, Ferber, and Free Speech Coalition v. Paxton. Each case has its rule, facts, holding, and dissent. Includes the Free Exercise, speech, prior restraint, and immoral speech checklists, along with synthesis tables.

First_Amendment_Drill.html.title: First Amendment Quick Drill
First_Amendment_Drill.html.description: 264 multiple-choice questions on every case and concept in the outline. They test what each case held, hypotheticals built on its facts, and how the doctrine applies. Filter by chapter or question type, shuffle the answers, and review only the ones you missed.

First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.title: First Amendment Flowcharts
First_Amendment_Flowcharts.html.description: Interactive decision charts for Chapters 1–6. A big-picture map shows how the Religion Clauses and the speech doctrines fit together, and eight charts walk through coercion, Free Exercise, the Establishment Clause and funding, the speech framework, incitement and fighting words, prior restraints, true threats and speech integral to crime, and immoral speech. Tap any box for a plain-English explanation, the cases behind it, and what to watch out for.

First_Amendment_Case_Files.html.title: First Amendment BAR style questions 1
First_Amendment_Case_Files.html.description: Bar-style application questions for Weeks 1–6 (Chapters 1–6). Each question sets out new facts, from compelled pledges and school prayer to protest livestreams, chatbot lawsuits, and age-verification laws, and asks you to apply the doctrine. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 113 outline items.
